title: Σῦς ἄγριος καὶ ἀλώπηξ
titleEn: The Wild Boar and the Fox
part: The Wild Boar and the Fox (Chambry 327)
source: Émile Chambry, Ésope: Fables, texte établi et traduit (Les Belles Lettres, Paris, 1927), fable 327. Text as printed, including Chambry's editorial punctuation (« »). Pronunciation: reconstructed Attic, after W. S. Allen, Vox Graeca. Romanization: standard classical transliteration (ē/ō; th/ph/ch; y for υ, u in diphthongs; h = rough breathing; ēi/āi/ōi for iota subscript; accents omitted).

sentences.t: Σῦς ἄγριος ἑστὼς παρά τι δένδρον τοὺς ὀδόντας ἠκόνα.
sentences.tr: Sys agrios hestōs para ti dendron tous odontas ēkona.
sentences.l: A wild boar, standing beside a tree, was whetting his tusks.
sentences.n: ἑστώς is the perfect participle of ἵστημι with present force, 'standing'. ὀδόντες are teeth in general, but in a boar they are the tusks. The imperfect ἠκόνα keeps the whetting going on while the fox comes up.

sentences.t: Ἀλώπεκος δὲ αὐτὸν ἐρομένης τὴν αἰτίαν δι’ ἣν, μηδενὸς αὐτῷ μήτε κυνηγέτου μήτε κινδύνου ἐφεστῶτος, τοὺς ὀδόντας θήγει, ἔφη· « Ἀλλ’ ἔγωγε οὐ ματαίως τοῦτο ποιῶ· ἐὰν γάρ με κίνδυνος καταλάβῃ, οὐ τότε περὶ τὸ ἀκονᾶν ἀσχοληθήσομαι, ἑτοίμοις δὲ οὖσι χρήσομαι. »
sentences.tr: Alōpekos de auton eromenēs tēn aitian di’ hēn, mēdenos autōi mēte kynēgetou mēte kindynou ephestōtos, tous odontas thēgei, ephē· « All’ egōge ou mataiōs touto poiō· ean gar me kindynos katalabēi, ou tote peri to akonan ascholēthēsomai, hetoimois de ousi chrēsomai. »
sentences.l: And a fox having asked him the reason for which, with nothing standing over him, neither hunter nor danger, he was sharpening his tusks, he said: « But I for my part do not do this idly; for if danger overtakes me, I shall not then be busied about the whetting, but shall use them ready. »
sentences.i: When a fox asked him why he was sharpening his tusks with no hunter and no danger anywhere near him, he said: « I am not doing this for nothing. If danger overtakes me, I shall have no leisure then for whetting; I shall have them ready and use them. »
sentences.n: Two genitive absolutes nest inside one another here — ἀλώπεκος … ἐρομένης for the fox's question, and μηδενὸς … ἐφεστῶτος inside it for the absence of any threat; the negative is μή rather than οὐ, the usual choice with a participle whose clause is conditional or generic rather than a plain statement of fact. ἐφίστημι in the perfect is the standing verb for a danger that is 'upon' a man. ἀσχολέομαι περί is to be taken up with a thing and so to have no leisure for anything else. ἔγωγε is ἐγώ with the emphatic particle, 'I at any rate'.

sentences.t: Ὁ λόγος διδάσκει δεῖν πρὸ τῶν κινδύνων τὰς παρασκευὰς ποιεῖσθαι.
sentences.tr: Ho logos didaskei dein pro tōn kindynōn tas paraskeuas poieisthai.
sentences.l: The story teaches that one must make one's preparations before the dangers.
sentences.n: δεῖν is the infinitive of δεῖ in indirect statement after διδάσκει. ποιεῖσθαι is middle, 'make for oneself', which with παρασκευή is the regular idiom for making one's own preparations.
